[b]Office of Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi[/b]

[u]Official Eid Message and Message of Goodwill to All | 10 Dhul Hijjah 1446 AH[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم [/i]

As salaamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh to all on this blessed day of Eid al-Adha. This is not just a day to celebrate and sacrifice our Qurbani to Allah because of custom or habit, or to dress nicely and go to the masjid because it is expected of us as Muslims. This is a day to increase our taqwa (awareness of Allah), good deeds, worship, and to remember the legacy and excellent of Prophet Ibrahim alayhi salam (upon him be peace). 

Of course, this is also a day of celebration and sharing the qurbani meat with our friends, families, neighbors and communities. Of course it is a day to dress nicely and attend the Eid prayer. 

But we must do all this things with the intention to please Allah swt first and foremost. Remember that Ibrahim alayhi Salam was commanded, as a test of faith, to sacrifice his son, we believe it to be Ismail alayhi salam (Ishmael to Jews and Christians), the Biblical narrative is that it was Ishaq alayhi Salam (Isaac). Either way, this was an enormous test of willpower and strength. He submitted to the command of Allah and his son was ransomed by a goat.

This story has been misrepresented by some as a cruel and barbaric command from Allah, that only an unjust God would demand a child to be sacrificed. But this was never the intention of Allah, the point was to test Ibrahim and Ismail in their dedication to Allah and His orders. The irony here is that many pagan peoples of the time did actually sacrifice their children. Allah swt forbade that with the exchange of Ismail alayhi Salam for a goat. Allah knows best.

We should also remember the sacrifices many made for the freedom of Baladullah from the tyrannical regime of Dhulmistan, the sacrifices our parents made to give us good lives, and all those who gave their lives for justice, liberation, and freedom in the world of all religions, races, ethnicities, and groups. 

We ask all the nations to remember the sacrifices their ancestors made for them to be independent, and we should also sacrifice our egos for the collective good, our sinful desires for righteousness, and sacrifice what is easy but leads to the corruption of our souls for what is more difficult but will, in shaa Allah, save us in this world and the next. Ameen.

[u][b]The New Era[/b][/u]

The Great Oceanice Republic teetered on the brink of transformation, its capital, Berlinwerk, rife with tension.  Vanklyis Adelais Herman, a renowned general turned reformist, found himself at the center of the unfolding events. His military precision, economic insights, and passionate speeches had garnered a dedicated following among soldiers and disenchanted citizens. For weeks, rumors of corruption and stagnation within the current regime had stoked unrest, paving the way for Hermans audacious move.  

Under the cover of darkness, Herman gathered with his trusted allies in a covert military command bunker on the fringes of Berlinwerk. Dim light illuminated the space, where maps and tactical outlines cluttered every surface.  

Tomorrow, we end the era of greed, Herman asserted, his voice firm as he indicated a red-circled section on the map: the Parliament Gate. The people deserve a leader who takes decisive action. We will provide them with that leader.  

Colonel Viktor Solzhar, Hermans second-in-command, nodded gravely. The units are positioned. By dawn, Berlinwerk will be ours.  

As dawn broke over the city, the rumbling of armored vehicles reverberated across cobblestone streets. Tanks, jeeps, and armed soldiers moved with military precision, establishing checkpoints and securing vital areas around the Parliament District. Citizens awoke to the sight of soldiers patrolling their neighborhoods, their presence both daunting and electrifying.  

At exactly 7:30 AM, Herman approached the Parliament Gate aboard an armored vehicle. Clad in an immaculate military uniform adorned with medals, he radiated confidence and authority. Behind him, a crowd had gatheredsome in admiration, others in quiet protest. Cameras from state and international media were trained on him as he raised a megaphone.  

People of Berlinwerk! Hermans voice resonated, cutting through the muted murmurs of the crowd. For too long, this nation has endured under the burden of corruption and stagnation. Today, we seize our future! The weak and corrupt shall fall, and a new Federation shall emergeone built on strength, prosperity, and freedom!  

The crowd erupted, a mix of cheers and gasps filling the air. Some hailed Herman as a champion, while others whispered concerns about tyranny. As his speech concluded, soldiers poured into the Parliament building. The operation was quick, efficient, and exact. Those who resisted were subdued, and soon, the halls of power fell under Hermans control.  
Inside the Parliament, Chancellor Hyram Eltrich, the beleaguered head of state, had barricaded himself with a handful of loyal guards. The sounds of gunfire and shouting grew nearer as Colonel Solzhar led the charge. Eltrich refused to yield, characterizing Herman as a traitor and a tyrant.  

This is not salvation, Eltrich spat as soldiers infiltrated the room. This is democracys demise.  
Herman entered shortly after, his presence dominating the room. He approached the captured Chancellor with deliberate steps, his gaze icy and unwavering.  

Your time is up, Eltrich, Herman stated, his voice lacking any sympathy. The people deserve more than your cowardice.  

Unyielding till the end, Eltrich shot back bitterly. You are no savior, Herman. You are but a tyrant in disguise.  
Dismissing the accusation, Herman ordered Eltrichs arrest. The ousted leader was led away, his fate uncertain but predetermined. As the old regime collapsed, Herman redirected his focus to the city.  

By noon, the Oceanice Republics flag was lowered from the Parliament Gate, replaced with a new emblem representing the dawn of Hermans envisioned Federation. Propaganda teams inundated the airwaves with visuals of the coup, casting it as a revolution for freedom. Across the capital, soldiers endeavored to restore order, while Herman addressed the nation from the steps of Parliament.  

This marks the start of a new era, he declared. An era of strength, unity, and prosperity. Together, we will construct a Republic that stands resilient against corruption and weakness!  
The crowd erupted in cheers, shouting, All Hail The New Führer. Vanklyis Adelais Herman stood amid the throngs, declaring, We shall no longer be known as the Oceanice Republic; our name will be the Adlerstahlince Republic.  

(Inside news spread to [nation]New Westmore[/nation][nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation][nation]United Hydronia[/nation][nation]Sikirsk[/nation][nation]Orphogron[/nation][nation]British Republic of Bob[/nation])
